messages:
Emily: Quick share — drafting a lightweight manager guide + self-review prompt set for the upcoming performance cycle. Idea is one page that managers can copy into 1:1s and use for calibration. Feedback please!
Jamal: Love it. Can you drop a super short checklist for managers? like 3 concrete things to do before calibration
Emily: Yep — thinking: 1) read the employee's self-review 2) prepare 2 examples (impact + ask) 3) bring calibration evidence (metrics, PRs). Short + actionable.
Sara: Also add an optional litmus test: "Would I bet on this person's next role in 12 months?" That helps with growth signals.
Alex: +1 on litmus test. Also suggest a quick rubric snippet for contribution vs. scope vs. leadership so managers have common language.
Emily: Here's a compact rubric snippet I drafted:
```
Contribution: delivered work quality & consistency (1-5)
Scope: complexity & cross-team impact (1-5)
Leadership: coaching, initiative, influence (1-5)
Evidence: 1-2 bullets linking to work
```
Use only if you need to differentiate — otherwise leave out.
Jamal: Can we get a plug-and-play self-review prompt set for ICs? Keep it short so people actually fill it.
Emily: Draft self-review (3 prompts + 1 growth question):
1) What were the 2-3 outcomes you drove this cycle? (link artifacts)
2) Where did you make the biggest tradeoff and why?
3) Two examples of feedback you acted on and the result
4) What skill or area do you want to grow next cycle? What support do you need?
+ optional: one sentence "What surprised you about your work?"
Oliver: Nice. For managers, maybe add a template line to surface blockers + recommended stretch for the person.
Emily: Good call. Manager comment template:
- Summary in 1 sentence
- Evidence using the rubric (numbers optional)
- One recommended focus for next cycle (skill, project, mentorship)
- Suggested calibration note (rating + whether promotable)
short and copy-ready.
Sara: Thumbs up. Anything for folks who are late-fillers or new hires with limited signal?
Emily: For <6mo hires: ask for most important contribution, learning highlights, and 2 supportive artifacts (PRs, docs). Managers should annotate "signal confidence: low/medium/high" with reason.
Alex: Can we add a tiny coaching script for managers who are giving constructive feedback? one-liners to keep it specific + forward-looking.
Emily: Sure — quick coaching script:
- Start: "I want to highlight something that went well: ___"
- Pivot: "One area to improve is ___ because ___"
- Next step: "Let's try X this quarter; I'll support by Y"
- Close: "Do you feel that's fair and doable?"
Jamal: Perfect. Last Q — format for the rollout doc. Suggest single page + a 2-slide deck for leads.
Emily: Plan: publish one-pager in handbook, 2-slide "how to" in the manager newsletter, and a sample copyable template in the self-review form. I'll prepare and ping for review next week.
people-bot: Reminder scheduled: "Performance cycle templates review" on 2201115800
Emily: Thanks — tagging @Sara @Alex @Jamal for final eyeballs before I push to handbook :thumbsup:
